{{Short description|French mathematician (born 1959)}}
'''Jean-Yves Chemin''' ({{IPA|fr|ʒɑ̃ iv ʃəmɛ̃}}; born 23 April 1959 in [[Rouen]]) is a French mathematician, specializing in nonlinear partial differential equations.

==Education and career==

Chemin studied from 1979 at the [[École normale supérieure de Cachan]] (now named the École normale supérieure Paris-Saclay) with [[Licentiate (degree)|licentiate]] in 1980 and ''[[agrégation]]'' in 1982.  At [[Paris-Sud University]] (Paris XI) he graduated in 1983 with [[Diplôme d'études approfondies]] (DEA) and in 1986 with doctorate in mathematics.<ref name=CV>{{cite web|title=CV. Chemin, Jean-Yves|website=Laboratorie Jacques Louis Lion, Université Pierre et Marie Curie|url=https://www.ljll.math.upmc.fr/~chemin/pdf/CV_JYC_W.pdf}}</ref> His doctoral dissertation ''Analyse microlocale précisée de solutions d’équations aux dérivées partielles non linéaires'' was supervised by [[Jean-Michel Bony]].<ref name="Bony1991">{{cite book|last1=Bony|first1=Jean-Michel|title=Microlocal Analysis and Applications|chapter=Analyse microlocale des équations aux dérivées partielles non linéaires|series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics|volume=1495|year=1991|pages=1–45|issn=0075-8434|doi=10.1007/BFb0085121|isbn=978-3-540-54948-2}}</ref> Chemin became in 1986 ''[[Academic ranks in France|Attaché de recherche]]'' at the [[École Polytechnique]] and in 1988 ''[[Chargé de recherche]]'' at the [[CNRS]]. In 1989 he received his [[habilitation]] with a thesis on singularities of nonlinear hyperbolic partial differential equations. From 1991 to 1995 he was ''[[Maître de conférences]]'' at the École Polytechnique. At [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] (Paris VI) in the Jacques-Louis Lions Laboratory, he was from 1993 to 2001 a professor and is since 2004 a professor. From 2001 to 2004 he was ''Professeur à temp plein'' (full-time non-tenured professor) at the École Polytechnique.<ref name=CV/>

His research deals with nonlinear partial differential equations describing physical systems that evolve over time. He focuses particularly on the [[Navier-Stokes equations]] and also works on the semi-linear Schrödinger equation and analysis on the [[Heisenberg group]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jean-Yves Chemin (homepage)|website=Laboratorie Jacques Louis Lion, Université Pierre et Marie Curie|url=https://www.ljll.math.upmc.fr/~chemin/}}</ref>

In 2012 he was awarded the ''Grand Prix Servant'' of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] for his work on the Navier-Stokes equations.<ref>[http://www.upmc.fr/fr/recherche/talents_et_decouvertes/prix_et_distinctions/2012/jean_yves_chemin_laureat_du_grand_prix_servant_2012.html Prix Servant]</ref>

From 1995 to 2001 he was a member of the [[Institut Universitaire de France]]. In 1995 he was awarded the ''Prix Langevin'' of the Académie des Sciences.<ref name=CV/>

Chemin was an invited speaker in 1994 at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] (ICM) in Zürich<ref>Chemin, Jean-Yves. ''Analyse microlocale et mécanique des fluides en dimension deux'' In: Srishti D. Chatterji (ed.): ''Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians. August 3–11, 1994, Zürich, Switzerland.'' vol. 2. Basel, Birkhäuser 1995, {{ISBN|3-7643-5153-5}}, pp. 1077–1085.</ref> and an invited speaker with [[Hajer Bahouri]] in 2002 at the ICM in Beijing.<ref>{{cite book|title=Proceedings of the ICM, Beijing, August 20–28, 2002|chapter=''Quasilinear wave equations and microlocal analysis'' by H. Bahouri and J.-Y. Chemin|volume=3|pages=141–154}} [https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0304390 arXiv preprint]</ref>

Chemin's doctoral students include [[Isabelle Gallagher]].
